description: Curtiss Robin c/n 428; built 1929; originally NC59H and later NR59H. As the "St. Louis Robin" it set the world flight-endurance record with Dale Jackson and Forest O'Brine over Missouri in July 1929 — 17 days 12 hours 17 minutes aloft. Acquired by Carlos Macaya and brought to Costa Rica in 2016 as a memorial to his father Román Macaya Lahmann; who flew a Curtiss Robin named Espíritu Tico from Oakland; California to Costa Rica on 5-6 October 1933; registered TI-BGZ and named Espíritu Tico II. Displayed for several years in front of the domestic terminal at San José Juan Santamaría (observed there February 2024 and described then as the oldest aircraft in Costa Rica). In May 2025 the Academia de Historia de la Aeronáutica y el Correo Aéreo took temporary custody; disassembled it and moved it to the Instituto de Formación Aeronáutica at Lagunilla de Heredia for restoration and permanent static exhibition. Non-airworthy. Status as of December 2025: disassembled; under restoration at IFA — NOT at the airport terminal.
